quote: Notwithstanding the foregoing, Client is not obligated to utilize the License and is free to acquire, develop, license or otherwise utilize any other hardware, software system, design, formula, procedure or trade secret to provide software and services similar to the ones provided by TrueLink hereunder, so long as such
rationale: The Agreement imposes no exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation on Client. Section 2(a) grants only a non-exclusive licence and expressly confirms that Client "is not obligated to utilize the License and is free to acquire, develop, license or otherwise utilize any other" comparable software or services (subject only to not infringing TrueLink IP and to the Section 10 confidentiality obligations) — that is the preferred position. Section 8 contains no restrictive covenant on Client, and the only exclusivity-flavoured language elsewhere (the non-exclusive licence of Credit Data in 8(d) and the "solely and exclusively" forum wording in Section 12) does not restrict Client's sourcing freedom. We note but do not flag Section 3(i), which requires Client to order a credit report from TrueLink for each borrower where underwriting approval is requested through a System using the Interface: that is a narrow condition on use of TrueLink's own Interface rather than a requirements or sole-supplier commitment, and Client remains free not to use the Interface at all. The cross-referenced Non-Competition Agreement is a separate document outside this review.

quote: 14. TERMINATION. Subject to Section 4 hereof, TrueLink will continue to provide the requested Hosting Services and Support Services until the last day of the month following the month in which Client provides TrueLink with a written notice of its election to terminate this Agreement.
rationale: The Agreement contains no liquidated damages, stipulated penalties or early-termination/minimum-fee charges payable by Client. Termination (§14) requires only a written notice with service continuing to the end of the following month, and non-renewal (§13) requires 30 days' notice, with no exit payment. Section 5 obliges Client to pay only fees for services actually requested (subject to a blank minimum monthly service fee during the term, which is an ordinary committed-volume charge, not a termination penalty), and the anti-spam covenant in §7 imposes no per-message charge on Client. This meets the preferred position (no Customer-payable liquidated damages or penalties), so no redline is warranted. Note for negotiation, not as a deviation: the monthly minimums in §5a are left blank and are carved out of Client's audit and dispute rights in §6 — we should confirm those figures and remove that carve-out under the pricing/audit rules.

quote: Notwithstanding the foregoing, Client is not obligated to utilize the License and is free to acquire, develop, license or otherwise utilize any other hardware, software system, design, formula, procedure or trade secret to provide software and services similar to the ones provided by TrueLink hereunder, so long as such
rationale: No non-compete, exclusivity or field-of-use restriction binds Client anywhere in the Agreement, so the preferred position is met. Section 2(a) goes further in our favour by expressly confirming Client is free to acquire, develop or license competing software and services (subject only to not infringing TrueLink's IP and to the Section 10 confidentiality obligations). The only Client covenants (Section 8) concern legal compliance, access control, no misrepresentation of underwriting decisions and no spamming — none restrict the businesses we may operate or the products we may buy or build. The single reference to a "Non-Competition Agreement" in Section 8(d) operates as a limitation on TrueLink's licence to use Credit Data, i.e. it restricts the Vendor and benefits us; the licence-grant wording tying Interface use to Client's consumer-finance origination business is a scope-of-licence limit, not a restraint on Client's business, and is noted only for completeness.

quote: 14. TERMINATION. Subject to Section 4 hereof, TrueLink will continue to provide the requested Hosting Services and Support Services until the last day of the month following the month in which Client provides TrueLink with a written notice of its election to terminate this Agreement.
rationale: Section 14 gives Client a unilateral, no-cause right to terminate on written notice, with services (and therefore charges) running only to the last day of the month following the notice month — roughly 30–60 days' notice, within our preferred 30-day band and well inside the fallback. No early-termination fee or penalty attaches: fees are invoiced monthly in arrears under Section 5(a) (invoices paid within 15 days of receipt), so there is no prepaid-fee exposure and the absence of an express pro-rata refund mechanic is immaterial here (noted, not flagged). On the other side, TrueLink has no mid-term convenience right: Section 13's early-termination triggers are Client breach/default (for cause), and the only other exit is a mutual 30-day notice of intent not to renew at the end of each one-year term — an end-of-term non-renewal right the fallback contemplates, exercisable equally by us, in a 12-month (not multi-year) auto-renewing term. The 30- rather than 90-day non-renewal notice is a minor sub-element and symmetric in our favour, so we would not spend leverage on it. No redline proposed.

quote: Client will be provided upon request with documentation supporting the amount charged (other than the minimum monthly fees listed in Section 4) and will be entitled to contest any charge
rationale: I searched the full agreement for audit, inspection, verification, records, books, monitoring and access rights and found no provision entitling TrueLink to audit, inspect or verify Client's usage, records or systems. Section 5/6 runs the other way: it gives Client (not the Vendor) the right to supporting documentation and to contest charges, and Section 2(e) gives Client real-time access to its own usage statistics and raw log files. Section 8(f) lets TrueLink implement technical mechanisms against spamming, but that is an operational control on the hosted Interface, not an audit right over Client's systems or records. Since no audit obligation binds us, there is nothing exceeding the preferred position (no more than annual, 30 days' notice, independent auditor, Vendor's cost, no system access) and no reason to introduce audit rights against ourselves. No redline proposed.

quote: TrueLink agrees that the costs for any Hosting Services will not increase for a period of one year from the date of this Agreement and that rates charged for Hosting Services will not exceed that charged by TrueLink to any other party.
rationale: The only most-favoured-nation language in the Agreement runs in our favour: in § 6 (DOCUMENTATION AND DISPUTES, p0047) TrueLink — the Vendor — undertakes that its Hosting Services rates "will not exceed that charged by TrueLink to any other party," plus a one-year price freeze. That is a Vendor-granted MFN benefiting Client, which the rule expressly welcomes and directs us not to redline. I checked the remainder of the document for a reverse-direction obligation: § 5 COMPENSATION (p0045) sets only Client's payment mechanics with no parity or price-matching covenant, and § 8 COVENANTS AND WARRANTIES OF CLIENT (p0051-p0058) contains no obligation for Client to extend TrueLink terms no less favourable than those given to third parties or to match third-party offers. Searches for "no less favorable", "most favored", and price-matching language returned no other hits. There is therefore no MFN burdening Customer, which meets the preferred position (no MFN obligation on Customer). No redline proposed. Noted only for the record: the Vendor MFN is limited to Hosting Services rates and has no audit or true-up mechanic to verify compliance, but that is an enhancement beyond this rule's scope rather than a deviation.

quote: 15. ASSIGNMENT OR TRANSFER. Neither party shall assign or transfer any of its rights under this Agreement without the prior written approval of the other party, except no such approval shall be required for an assignment to a financially responsible affiliate.
rationale: Section 15 is the only assignment provision in the Agreement. It bars assignment by either party absent the other's prior written approval, with the sole exception of an assignment to a "financially responsible affiliate." It therefore fails the fallback on two material terms: (i) there is no successor/M&A carve-out, so a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all of Client's assets would require TrueLink's consent — the playbook treats a Customer assignment restriction with no M&A carve-out as walk-away territory; and (ii) the consent standard is unqualified, not "not to be unreasonably withheld," so TrueLink may refuse arbitrarily (including on our affiliate transfers, where "financially responsible" is itself a judgment call). There is no competitor restriction on TrueLink's side. On the positive side, no change-of-control termination or re-pricing right exists anywhere in the document (searches for "change of control" and "merger" returned nothing, and the term/termination provisions at Sections 13-14 contain no such trigger), so only the assignment carve-outs need fixing. The redline adds the affiliate/successor carve-out for Client, subjects TrueLink's assignment to our consent (not unreasonably withheld) and bars assignment to a Client competitor, and confirms that a Client change of control is not an assignment and gives TrueLink no exit.

ops.text: e. Client Ownership. quote: d. Ownership. Notwithstanding the license granted under section 2.1, TrueLink retains all of its ownership and license rights in the Interface.
rationale: The only ownership provision is Section 2(d), which preserves TrueLink's rights in the Interface (acceptable under the rule) but says nothing about our side. No clause anywhere confirms that Client retains title to Client Content, Client's Intellectual Property (a defined term at p0012 that is never operative) or borrower/loan data, and nothing addresses ownership of the results of the Support Services we pay for. Section 10(b)/(c) only makes Client's IP and "all results of the Hosting and Support Services" confidential, which is not ownership, and p0078 addresses domains and Client Content only on discontinuance of hosting. That leaves the rule's preferred and fallback positions unmet, so we insert a reciprocal ownership subsection with a licence back for any embedded TrueLink IP and an express no-joint-ownership statement. Noted but not separately flagged: Section 8(d) grants TrueLink a broad non-exclusive licence over the narrowly defined Credit Data (raw, aged repository data excluding Client Proprietary Information), which is a licence rather than an assignment and is limited by the Non-Competition Agreement; our insert is expressed to be subject to it.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] The Agreement gives us no exit rights, so we have added a transition and data-return paragraph: up to six months of assistance at TrueLink's then-current rates, return of our data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days of expiration or termination, and certified deletion thereafter. If six months is too long, we can work with 90 days of assistance provided the 30-day export remains.

ops.text: 14a. TRANSITION ASSISTANCE AND RETURN OF DATA. Upon expiration or termination of this Agreement for any reason, TrueLink shall (a) at Client's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at TrueLink's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days of such expiration or termination, return to Client all Client Content, Client Proprietary Information and other data of Client in TrueLink's possession or control in a standard machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete all such Client Content, Client Proprietary Information and data from its systems and certify such deletion to Client in writing.

proposal.summary: Insert Section 14a requiring transition assistance, return of Client data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certified deletion.

quote: 14. TERMINATION. Subject to Section 4 hereof, TrueLink will continue to provide the requested Hosting Services and Support Services until the last day of the month following the month in which Client provides TrueLink with a written notice of its election to terminate this Agreement.
rationale: This is a hosting agreement in which TrueLink holds Client Content and borrower/loan data, but neither the Term (Section 13) nor Termination (Section 14) provision, nor the Confidentiality section (Section 10), gives Client any exit rights. Section 13 only puts the burden on Client to arrange a new name server within 30 days and a new hosting environment within 60 days, and Section 14 merely runs services to month-end; there is no obligation on TrueLink to provide transition assistance, to return or export Client data in a usable format, or to delete it afterwards. No such clause exists anywhere in the document, so the rule's expected clause is missing (below even the fallback of 90 days' assistance plus 30-day export). We propose inserting the preferred language as new Section 14a, which will survive termination under Section 24.

verification.notes: The Agreement contained no transition or data-return mechanic; the inserted Section 14a is a concise, self-contained clause that completes every preferred element: 6 months' assistance at then-current rates, 30-day return in a standard machine-readable format measured from expiry/termination, and deletion with written certification thereafter. The "at Client's request" condition attaches only to transition assistance; the data return, deletion and certification duties remain unconditional, so the request condition does not swallow the mandatory return. No unrelated term is altered: Sections 13 and 14 are untouched, the new paragraph is numbered 14a, and it uses existing defined terms (Client, TrueLink, Client Content, Client Proprietary Information) without introducing undefined terms or contradictions. The qualifier "reasonable" before transition assistance is a customary softener that does not defeat the duty or its duration; it is a rationale-level note rather than a deviation.
